name: Seti Square and Town Center
description: Mestia's central hub around Seti Square, where guesthouses, cafes, ATMs, the tourism office, and morning marshrutka and 4x4 drivers all cluster. This is the most connected, convenient base in town and the natural place to organize treks, find a meal, or catch a shared ride to the trailheads.
vibe: Bustling by local standards, practical, social
bestFor: First-time visitors and trekkers who want convenience
pros: Best access to transport and services
Easiest place to find guesthouses and food
cons: Busiest and least tranquil in peak season
Less of the timeless village feel

name: Lagami and Lanchvali Tower Quarters
description: The historic residential quarters on Mestia's edges, where the famous Svan defensive stone tower-houses cluster most densely. Quieter and more atmospheric than the square, these neighborhoods put you among centuries-old koshki and family guesthouses, a short walk from the center yet steeped in the town's UNESCO-listed heritage.
bestFor: Culture lovers wanting atmosphere over convenience

name: Hatsvali Ski Area Side
description: The forested slopes southwest of Mestia leading up to the small Hatsvali ski area and its viewpoints toward Ushba. A quieter, higher base with a handful of guesthouses and a chairlift, best for those who want easy trail access in summer or the modest winter ski scene right outside the door.
bestFor: Skiers and hikers wanting slope-side quiet
pros: Direct access to slopes and viewpoints
cons: Removed from town services and dining

name: Ushguli
tagline: The highest inhabited village in Europe
description: A cluster of ancient tower-filled hamlets at around 2,100m, roughly a rough two-hour 4x4 ride beyond Mestia and one of the highest continuously inhabited settlements in Europe. The classic end point of the Mestia-to-Ushguli trek, sitting beneath Mount Shkhara with jaw-dropping Svan scenery and heritage.
bestFor: Adventurers seeking the ultimate off-grid Svan experience
cons: Hard rough road access, often cut off in winter
